QUESTION 16 – What is the main difference between severe asthma and uncontrolled asthma, according to current guidelines?
A) Uncontrolled asthma occurs only in patients who do not use any type of treatment.
B) Severe asthma is defined exclusively by the presence of frequent exacerbations and the need for hospitalization.
C) Severe asthma persists with symptoms and increased risk despite optimized treatment use, while uncontrolled asthma may be associated with poor adherence or inadequate treatment.
D) Severe asthma is always a temporary and self-limited condition, unlike uncontrolled asthma.
E) The two conditions are the same.

QUESTION 21 – Regarding the updates in GINA 2025 for asthma management, select the correct alternative.
A) GINA 2025 again recommended the isolated use of SABA for patients with mild asthma, without the need for inhaled corticosteroids.
B) The use of biologic therapies became indicated for all patients with persistent asthma, regardless of phenotype.
C) GINA 2025 reinforces that the combination of formoterol + inhaled corticosteroid can be used both as maintenance treatment and as relief in mild to moderate asthma.
D) Monitoring of lung function became unnecessary in patients stable for more than 12 months.
E) Stepped treatment was replaced by a uniform treatment model for all patients with asthma.

QUESTION 19 – Regarding Occupational Asthma (OA), it is correct to state that:
A) The intensity of exposure is not an important risk factor for the development of OA.
B) Smoking is considered a protective factor.
C) Exhaled Nitric Oxide (FeNO) has a well-established role in the diagnosis of OA.
D) The benefit of reducing the level of exposure is equivalent to complete removal from exposure to the causative agent.
E) When an individual becomes sensitized to an occupational agent, even low levels of exposure (within legally permitted limits) can trigger severe bronchospasm

QUESTION 29 – Asthma is a noncommunicable respiratory disease that affects about 350 million people worldwide. Regarding the endotypes and phenotypes of asthma, it is INCORRECT to state that:
A) Asthma with a Th2-high phenotype was first based on atopic predisposition in combination with any of the following biomarkers for Th2 immune activation: serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) ≥100 IU/mL, blood eosinophil count ≥300/μL and
B) T2 immune responses include IgE- and allergen-mediated hypersensitivity, chemotaxis of mast cells, eosinophils and basophils, and remodeling of the airway epithelium.
C) The late-onset eosinophilic asthma phenotype usually begins in adulthood, occurs mainly through a T2 inflammatory response, affecting a significant proportion of elderly patients, usually a more severe disease, with lower lung function, increased eosinophils in blood and sputum.
D) T2-low asthma is characterized by activation of non-T2 inflammatory pathways, with symptom onset in adulthood, and is often associated with obesity, cigarette smoke exposure, lower bronchodilator reversibility.
E) The asthma phenotype associated with the elderly has no direct relationship with changes in lung structure present in elderly patients, such as airway narrowing, reduced lung compliance or alveolar dilation.

35 Asthma is a disease characterized by episodes of airway obstruction and increased airway responsiveness, accompanied by an inflammatory reaction. Asthma is one of the most common chronic diseases associated with morbidity and mortality. Regarding asthma, select the correct statement.
(A) A significant proportion of asthma heritability is related to atopy, which is a genetic tendency to produce specific IgA in response to allergens.
(B) The inflammatory infiltrate is basically composed of neutrophils. The infiltrate of eosinophils and mast cells is seen in more severe disease.
(C) Greater airway thickness has no relationship with asthma severity, as it is a universal finding due to inflammatory attacks.
(D) One of the possible causes of severe bronchospasm may be mediated by decreased local nitric oxide levels, which is frequently documented.
(E) Type 2 inflammatory reaction, associated with interleukins 4, 5 and 13, is the most common form of stimulus for increased bronchial reactivity.

36. Female patient, 20 years old, diagnosed with asthma, uses salbutamol spray when she feels short of breath, and improves, but lately has been having shortness of breath at rest and on minimal exertion, even using salbutamol spray 5x/day. She reports that 1 year ago she had a severe asthma attack and was taken to the emergency room and was admitted to the ICU and intubated. She is a smoker, 5 pack-years, but stopped 1 week ago because her shortness of breath worsened. Select the correct alternative.
(A) This patient should receive a prescription for formoterol and budesonide, salbutamol spray as a rescue drug, and be referred for spirometry, advised to continue not smoking. And return when the test is ready.
(B) This patient should be referred for treatment in the emergency room. And advised to carry out treatment properly.
(C) She should be vaccinated (against COVID-19, H1N1 and pneumonia), buy a pulse oximeter to monitor O2 saturation (a warning sign for her), and use formoterol 12 mcg and budesonide 400 mcg 3x/day, salbutamol spray as rescue during attacks.
(D) She should receive guidance on the severity of her disease, although the clinical picture she had (ICU admission) is unlikely to occur again.
(E) If necessary at first, this patient should undergo endotracheal intubation (mechanical ventilation), even without altered level of consciousness.

37. Male patient, professional athlete, with asthma, presented, in the last 4 weeks, daytime symptoms 2x/week. He has no limitation for his daily activities, needs relief medication 2x/week. Select the correct alternative.
(A) The patient's asthma is partially controlled.
(B) The patient's asthma is controlled, as it does not interfere with his daily activities.
(C) The patient has uncontrolled asthma.
(D) This patient may use only relief medication (salbutamol spray).
(E) This patient should use inhaled corticosteroid and salbutamol spray; if necessary, suspend his training until the next spirometry.

43. Select the correct alternative.
(A) Occupational asthma and work-related asthma are the same disease.
(B) Individuals whose professional activity involves high-molecular-weight agents do not develop work-related asthma.
(C) The incidence and prevalence of occupational asthma do not depend on genetic predisposition.
(D) In adult patients with asthma initiated or worsened during work, the diagnosis of work-related asthma should be considered.
(E) The treatment of occupational asthma is similar to non-occupational asthma. But measurement of IgE in nasal secretion, which should be monitored in these patients, drops drastically within a few days after removal from the causative agent.

43. Regarding the diagnosis of asthma, select the correct alternative:
A) Peak expiratory flow is an essential method for monitoring, but not for initial diagnosis.
B) The reversibility test with bronchodilators is used to identify irreversible airway obstruction.
C) Spirometry confirms the diagnosis only in asymptomatic patients.
D) The diagnosis of asthma is confirmed only by the presence of wheezing on physical examination.

48) Male patient, 44 years old, reports a diagnosis of 'severe asthma' in 2017. On the day of the consultation, he complained of cough, mainly at night, dyspnea on exertion, such as tidying up the house, rhinorrhea and diffuse wheezing, even while using inhaled formoterol and budesonide 1x/day. PMH: Denies asthma in childhood. Diagnosis of chronic rhinitis and sinusitis, using nasal budesonide 32 mcg, 1 spray in each nostril 'as needed'. Allergens: Reports allergy to mold and dust. SH: Former smoker for 10 years, 20 pack-years. Has 3 cats and 2 dogs at home. Caregiver. FH: Mother with asthma, in addition to sister, 2 paternal uncles, grandmother and cousins. Is the diagnosis of 'severe asthma' correct in this patient?
a) Yes, because he is very symptomatic.
b) No, because this definition is retrospective.
c) Yes, because he has untreated comorbidities.
d) No, because the patient is in contact with allergens.

50) Male patient, 44 years old, reports a diagnosis of 'severe asthma' in 2017. On the day of the consultation, he complained of cough, mainly at night, dyspnea on exertion, such as tidying up the house, rhinorrhea and diffuse wheezing, even while using inhaled formoterol and budesonide 1x/day. Regarding the meanings associated with mild to moderate diffuse bronchial wall thickening in a patient with asthma, indicate true (T) or false (F) for the statements below, and then select the option that presents the correct sequence.
( ) Indicates an acute phase of inflammation.
( ) May indicate a greater risk of airway remodeling.
( ) Is usually present in more advanced phases of the disease.

a) (F); (F); (F); (T).
b) (F); (T); (T); (F).

51) Male patient, 44 years old, reports a diagnosis of 'severe asthma' in 2017. Question 29 Respiratory tract infections can have distinct pathophysiological spectra (viral, bacterial, polymicrobial infections, infections of an 'adjacent organ' with pulmonary repercussions) and the pulmonologist must know how to grade severity, anatomical extent and appropriate therapeutic indication. On this subject, analyze the following statements.
I. In community-acquired pneumonias, the use of biomarkers such as procalcitonin can help reduce unnecessary antibiotic use, especially in viral cases, when used together with clinical and radiological evaluation.
II. In acute bronchitis in a patient without COPD, without persistent fever and without tachycardia/systemic manifestations, empirical antibiotic use is considered the gold standard for preventing progression to pneumonia.
III. Respiratory viral infections can trigger exacerbation of previous chronic diseases of the airways and lung parenchyma, including asthma and COPD, even in the absence of secondary bacterial infection.
Select the alternative that presents only the CORRECT statements.
(A) I, II and III.
(B) I.
(C) I and III.
(D) II.

Question 34 Childhood asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease of the airways characterized by bronchial hyperresponsiveness, reversible airflow obstruction and recurrent episodes of wheezing, cough and dyspnea. Diagnosis and management depend on detailed clinical evaluation, functional tests and long-term control strategies. Considering pathophysiology, risk factors and management of asthma in children, analyze the following statements and select the true one.
(A) Regular use of inhaled corticosteroids in children with moderate to severe persistent asthma reduces airway inflammation and prevents exacerbations.
(B) Childhood asthma is predominantly caused by bacterial infections, and eosinophilic inflammation is irrelevant for disease severity and monitoring.
(C) Environmental control and allergen avoidance do not impact the frequency or severity of symptoms in asthmatic children.
(D) Lung function measured by spirometry is only useful in adults and has no utility in children with suspected asthma, and may be ignored in clinical follow-up.

35. Asthma is the most frequent chronic disease in childhood in all countries worldwide. Analyze the statements below regarding its diagnosis:
1. In children, spirometry, measurement of bronchial hyperresponsiveness (BHR) and tests that measure inflammation in the lower airways aid in the diagnosis of asthma.
2. Spirometry before and after bronchodilator (BD) use should be routinely performed in all children with suspected asthma.
3. Allergy evaluation by total IgE measurement, immediate-reading skin tests or serum specific IgE can determine whether one or more allergens are involved in the pathophysiology of asthma.
4. These characteristics or manifestations can occur in mild, moderate and severe attacks (exacerbations) and manifest intermittently or persistently (between attacks).
Select the alternative that indicates all correct statements.
a. Only statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct.
b. Only statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct.
c. Only statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct.
d. Only statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct.
e. Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4 are correct.

34 The Global Strategy for Asthma Management and Prevention (GINA) recommends the use of biologics in severe asthma. Recently, some of these biologics have been incorporated into the SUS (Unified Health System). Select the option that indicates the biologic recommended by GINA for severe eosinophilic asthma.
(A) Secukinumab.
(B) Omalizumab.
(C) Tezepelumab.
(D) Tocilizumab.
(E) Mepolizumab.

44 A 36-year-old patient with asthma presents characteristic asthma symptoms 2x/week, in addition to exacerbations 3x/year. According to the latest version of the Global Strategy for Asthma Management and Prevention (GINA, 2023), select the option that presents the most appropriate therapeutic approach.
(A) Salbutamol as needed.
(B) Formoterol/Budesonide every 12 hours and as needed in case of symptoms.
(C) Formoterol/Budesonide every 12 hours, Tiotropium 1x/day, Salbutamol as needed.
(D) Eosinophil and IgE measurement, refer for use of biologic.
(E) Budesonide every 12 hours and as needed.

Question 45 Asthma treatment aims to achieve and maintain current disease control, as well as prevent future risks. This implies a personalized approach, including, in addition to pharmacological treatment, patient education, a written action plan, training in the use of the inhaler device and review of inhalation technique at each visit. According to the Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA – 2021), asthma control can be divided into five steps, varying according to patient age. The preferred treatment for asthma control and rescue, in patients > 12 years of age, in Step 4 of the Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA – 2021), is:
A) High dose of inhaled corticosteroid + long-acting β2-agonist + Tiotropium.
B) Moderate dose of inhaled corticosteroid for control and short-acting β2-agonist for relief.
C) Moderate dose of inhaled corticosteroid + Formoterol for control and low dose of inhaled corticosteroid + Formoterol for relief.
D) Low dose of inhaled corticosteroid + long-acting β2-agonist + Montelukast for control and short-acting β2-agonist for relief.
E) Moderate dose of inhaled corticosteroid + long-acting β2-agonist + Montelukast for control and low dose of inhaled corticosteroid + Formoterol for relief.

Question 62 The advent of biologics has revolutionized the treatment of patients with severe refractory asthma. These agents act on different components of the inflammatory cascade; they are indicated for specific phenotypes. They are predictors of a good response to Anti-IL5/Anti-IL5R medications, EXCEPT:
A) Eosinophilia.
B) Nasal polyposis.
C) Onset of asthma in adult life.
D) Higher number of exacerbations in the last year.
E) Ratio of forced expiratory volume in the first second / forced vital capacity < 50%.

Question 70 The heterogeneous and complex nature of severe asthma signals different disease phenotypes, whose identification may represent an opportunity for successful targeted therapy. Given the above, it is correct to state that:
A) The eosinophilic phenotype is the most common.
B) The T2-low endotype corresponds to most cases of severe asthma.
C) The paucigranulocytic phenotype is found in most treatment-naive asthmatics.
D) IL-4 acts mainly by promoting remodeling of the smooth muscle of the airways.
E) IL-13 has as its main role helping the recruitment, maturation and survival of eosinophils.

Question 80 Occupational asthma is a disease defined by the presence of asthma symptoms and reversible airflow obstruction and/or bronchial hyperreactivity due to conditions attributable to the work environment. Regarding occupational asthma, select the INCORRECT statement.
A) Smoking is a well-defined risk factor for some types of occupational asthma.
B) Serial measurement of peak expiratory flow on spirometry is poorly specific for its diagnosis.
C) The specific bronchial provocation test is considered the gold standard for the diagnosis of occupational asthma.
D) Serial spirometric measurements of peak expiratory flow have high sensitivity for the diagnosis of occupational asthma.
E) Occupational asthma due to sensitizers is more frequently associated with an eosinophilic phenotype than asthma aggravated or exacerbated by work.

a) Chronic expectoration
b) Symptoms are triggered by exposure to allergens, exercise, climate changes, laughing, crying or respiratory irritants such as smoke or strong odors
c) Worsening of symptoms at night or in the morning
d) Variation in symptom intensity over time

32 A 35-year-old woman with asthma, already followed for five years in a specialized outpatient clinic, presenting in the last two years asthma attacks requiring emergency room visits on two occasions, and in the last year she needed three courses of systemic corticosteroids. She has allergic rhinitis. Her regular medications: formoterol/budesonide 12/400 mcg, 1 puff every eight hours; tiotropium 5 mcg daily; salbutamol 2 puffs every 12 hours; montelukast sodium 10 mg once daily; nasal budesonide 100 mcg every twelve hours, after nasal irrigation with saline. She brought tests performed outside the crisis period, more than sixty days without systemic corticosteroid use, with normal blood count and IgE level of 453 IU/ml. Residential and workplace investigation was performed and was negative for antigen contact. Gastroesophageal reflux disease and sleep apnea were ruled out. Based on this hypothetical situation, regarding the management aimed at controlling this patient's disease, select the correct alternative.
(A) maintain medications, adding omalizumab
(B) maintain medications, adding benralizumab
(C) discontinue tiotropium and start dupilumab
(D) maintain medications and add prednisone 5 mg per day, permanently
(E) discontinue all inhaled medications and start triple inhaled therapy in a single device

58) Asthma treatment often involves the use of bronchodilator medications that act on different receptors in the airways. Regarding bronchodilators, analyze the statements below and give values True (T) or False (F).
( ) Salmeterol is a short-acting beta 2-agonist bronchodilator.
( ) Glycopyrronium bromide is a short-acting antimuscarinic bronchodilator.
( ) Umeclidinium is a long-acting beta 2-agonist bronchodilator.
( ) Indacaterol is a long-acting antimuscarinic bronchodilator.
Select the alternative that presents the correct sequence from top to bottom:
a) T - F - F - F
b) F - F - F - F
c) F - T - T - F
d) T - F - T - T
e) T - T - T - F

QUESTION 15 – Analyze the statements below about asthma:
I. For spirometric diagnosis, we consider a positive bronchodilator test when there is an increase in FEV1 of at least 200 ml and at least 7% of predicted.
II. Environmental control measures, influenza and pneumococcal vaccination and use of inhaled corticosteroids are prescribed at all stages of asthma treatment.
III. Before stepping up asthma treatment, it is recommended to review inhalation technique, treatment adherence and control of environmental exposure.
IV. Emotional stress, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, temperature changes and sinusopathy are not triggering factors for asthma exacerbation.
Which are correct?
A) Only I and II.
B) Only II and III.
C) Only III and IV.
D) Only I, II and III.
E) Only I, III and IV.

QUESTION 35 – Analyze the statements below about biologics in severe asthma:
I. Omalizumab, a humanized anti-IgE monoclonal antibody, reduced exacerbations by approximately 25% when compared with placebo.
II. Mepolizumab inhibits the binding of Interleukin-5 to its receptors on eosinophils and is indicated in Brazil for the treatment of severe eosinophilic asthma with eosinophilia >400 cells/μL.
III. Tezepelumab, due to its corticosteroid-sparing effect, is indicated for severe asthma, especially in patients who are chronic users of oral corticosteroids.
Which are correct?
A) Only I.
B) Only II.
C) Only I and II.
D) Only I and III.
E) I, II and III.
